figureTime._comment: v57 §3.7/§3.8 — TWO CLOCKS PER FIGURE, both read out of the captures in cowork/reference/dfas-2026/ and neither taken from any directive. effectiveFrom/To is the RATE clock: when this amount took effect. authorityExpiresOn is the AUTHORITY clock: when the legal power to pay this entitlement at all lapses unless Congress renews it, from the DFAS Duration of Authority table (page updated April 7, 2026). They are independent — a rate can be perfectly current while its authority is weeks from lapsing, which is exactly the situation below. authorityPermanent is NEVER a default: absence of an expiry means notEstablished, not permanence.

payTable._authority: Basic pay does not appear on the Duration of Authority table — it is permanent statutory pay, not a bonus or incentive requiring renewal. But ABSENCE IS NOT PERMANENCE (§3.8b): nothing captured states that affirmatively, so the authority clock is NOT ESTABLISHED rather than permanent.

limits.rothCatchupWageThreshold._note: The $150,000 is the notice's 'Roth catch-up wage threshold for 2025' — prior-year wages — applied to determine which 2026 catch-ups must be Roth. The window records the year it GOVERNS (2026), which is how the notice frames it.

basicPayCapO7AndAboveMonthly._note: RULED state 4a (user ruling 2026-08-06, directive build 57 §3, adopting Cowork's recommendation): the prior published value, carried forward, not yet confirmed. This note argued 4a from the start ('It DOES change with time, so still-in-force would be a lie; but the military pay raise is not the mechanism that moves it, so scaling it by the raise is also a lie'); the model could not express 4a for an annual figure until valueCarriedForward existed, and now note and model agree. NUANCE, recorded rather than hidden: the captured 2026 DFAS table's O-9/O-10 cells are capped AT this value and matched in the build-55 verify run — the amount has operational 2026 evidence even though no capture STATES it as the ceiling with a window. The ruling stands; the evidence is logged for a future refinement.

basicPayCapO6AndBelowMonthly._note: Same ruling as its sibling above — and here 4a is unambiguous: this value appears NOWHERE in the captured pages (no O-6 cell reaches the Level V cap in 2026, so nothing prints it), making 'not yet confirmed' simply true.

notes: rev 12 (build 57, discrepancy sweep): hostile fire / imminent danger pay finally has a transcribed source. It had NONE — carried on unrecorded authority through every round since it was added — and the gap was recorded in its own clock note rather than hidden, which is how the sweep found it. FMR Vol 7A Ch 10 para 2.1.1 states the rate outright and Table 1-10 note 3 corroborates it in the app's own use, the officer combat-zone ceiling. The amount was already correct; only its provenance changed. rev 11 (build 57 SS5.1): the flying-HDIP table is verified against the FMR at last — every grade matches, the FMR's stated effective date is transcribed onto both flying figures' clocks, and the citation carries the volume, chapter, table, page and file hash. It also surfaced a conflict the register had been calling 'not comparable': the current FMR edition's own printed table disagrees with DFAS's current service pages, grade by grade, and the FMR itself points readers to DFAS for current rates. ESCALATED under ruling D-17, not resolved — the figures in this file are unchanged, and the sources entry states both sides with their shapes. rev 10 (build 57 SS2 and SS3): the seven-contradiction repair. The five IRS limits gain their effective windows, transcribed from Notice 2025-67's own year designation (see the sources entry with the file hash) — they now resolve published-current for 2026 instead of 'projected', which falsely claimed the app computed numbers the IRS published. The two statutory ceilings are RULED state 4a (user ruling of 6 August 2026, adopting Cowork's recommendation): prior published value, carried forward, not yet confirmed — valueCarriedForward added to their clocks, official flipped to false, and the note-vs-model disagreement this file carried since rev 9 is closed with the model agreeing with the note. rev 9 (build 56, v57 SS3.6): every FIGURE moved out of these notes and into `sources`. The superseded HALO figure now sits in a `sources` entry marked with supersededValue/supersededBy/supersededOn — a field, not a word in prose, so a reader can separate current from superseded without parsing English, and so the validator can refuse to let a superseded entry stand as evidence for a live figure. These notes keep the story; `sources` keeps the numbers. rev 8 (build 55): HALO / MILITARY FREE FALL PARACHUTE DUTY CORRECTED — the shipped figure was too LOW. Our source was a superseded FMR edition and our copy of it was simply old; DFAS's current published page is later and prints more. The ruling (DECISIONS.md D-17) is narrow: where our source is a superseded FMR edition and DFAS's current page is later, the DFAS page is sufficient authority. It is NOT a general licence — two current sources disagreeing, or DFAS against a current FMR edition, still escalates to the user. MEMBER-VISIBLE AND IN THE MEMBER'S FAVOUR: hdipParachuteHalo is an extra-pay category on the Pay screen, so a member on military free-fall status had been planning against LESS contribution room than DFAS publishes. The correction opens room; NOBODY WAS EVER OVER-CREDITED. Found by tool/verify_dfas.dart comparing every shipped figure against the captured DFAS pages — everything else matched exactly. NOT corrected in the same pass and deliberately still absent: DFAS also publishes an Army-specific static-line rate with its own effective window which this file does not carry. See EXTERNAL-DATA-REGISTER.md — it is a schema/shape change (branch- and date-aware rates) rather than a transcription, and it is knowingly deferred rather than undiscovered. rev 7 (v57 SS3): basicPayCapMonthly RENAMED to basicPayCapO7AndAboveMonthly. Value, official flag and source all unchanged — a naming correction only. The old name read as a single universal ceiling on basic pay; there are two, and this one binds O-7 through O-10 (Executive Schedule Level II) while basicPayCapO6AndBelowMonthly binds O-6 and below (Level V). A name that hides which grades a ceiling applies to is how the wrong one gets used. Neither is ever scaled by the raise. rev 6 (v56 SS2, audit D-19): CATCH-UP CORRECTION. catchUp50 carried a prototype-era estimate flagged official:false and was later read as a fact. The published CY2026 figure is transcribed from IRS Notice 2025-67 and cited in `sources`. A member aged 50 or over planning against the old estimate left tax-advantaged room unused every year — silently, and unrecoverably after 31 December. Note the direction, because it is why it survived: the estimate was CONSERVATIVE, so nothing overshot, nothing was refused, and no error ever fired. A wrong number that fails safely is a wrong number that survives. catchUp60to63 is unchanged — the same notice states this higher limit remains at its prior value — and is now flagged official:true, which it always should have been. NOTE FOR ANYONE TEMPTED BY THE STATUTE: the super catch-up is defined as the greater of a fixed statutory floor or one and a half times the standard catch-up, and that computation does NOT reproduce the published super catch-up. The two disagree. Transcribe, never derive. rev 5 (v52-3): sgli block added — the VA-published SGLI premium table, transcribed verbatim and carried as printed rather than derived from the rate; validation rejects any level that disagrees with the stated rate. Source and page date are in `sources`. rev 4 (v45 SS2): the statutory ceiling on monthly basic pay added, 37 U.S.C. 203(a)(2) — O-7 through O-10 basic pay limited to Executive Schedule Level II. It restates, with its rule, the in-file official figure whose capped O-9/O-10 rows are already transcribed in this file's payTable; the figure itself lives in basicPayCapO7AndAboveMonthly rather than being repeated here. rev 3: axisDateLabel on the AvIP byYears tables (v25 SS4, additive). Raise per NDAA FY26; limits per IRS Notice 2025-67, both cited in `sources`.

sgli.source: VA, "Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance (SGLI)", https://www.va.gov/life-insurance/options-eligibility/sgli/ — premium rate table transcribed verbatim; page states "Last updated: September 19, 2025". Coverage is offered to $500,000 in $50,000 increments at 5 cents per $1,000 per month, plus $1.00 per month for Traumatic Injury Protection (TSGLI). VERIFIED FIRST-PARTY 2026-08-06 (v57 §9.1): va.gov answered 200 — it is not DFAS and does not refuse scripted requests — and the page was captured to cowork/reference/va-2026/sgli.html, sha256 bc63e9e343e1194c28fb068caa30b72a833b192e221135ba21c15b441eda9415. All ten coverage levels, the 0.05 per-$1,000 rate, the $1.00 TSGLI charge and the 2025-09-19 date match the live page exactly. The prior 'Cowork to verify' clause is discharged.
